I been farming this land 50 years. Same wheat after maize, maize after wheat, like my father did, like everyone around here does.

My 8.7 mu, I split it simple — wheat goes in October after the maize comes off, maize goes in June after I cut the wheat. No changing that.

For seed, I go to the same dealer in town. For maize I buy the hybrid seed, everyone buys hybrid now, the old seeds don't yield. Wheat I buy the improved variety, whichever bag the dealer says is selling good this year. My neighbor Old Wang had good wheat last year so I ask him what he planted.

Fertilizer I think in bags. For wheat base I put one bag of the 二铵 (DAP, 50 jin — 25 kg) per mu when I plow, then come spring when the wheat greens up I throw urea, maybe 40-50 jin per mu. That's what works. If I put less I worry the yield drops, and a bad harvest hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I add some potassium too, maybe 20 jin per mu, the dealer sells a bag.

Maize I put less base fertilizer, the soil already has something left from wheat. One bag compound 复合肥 at sowing, then urea at knee-high stage, maybe 40 jin. 

Water — wheat needs watering. I water before winter so it goes through the cold, then green-up water in spring, then one more when the grain fills. Three times. My well works fine. Maize in summer the rain usually comes, I only water once or twice if it's dry, mostly at tasseling.

Pesticide — wheat I spray once for weeds in spring, once for aphids before harvest. Maize I spray once for the borer worm, sometimes twice if I see them bad.

Tillage — after maize comes off I rotary the stalks in and plant wheat right away. After wheat I don't plow, I just drill the maize straight into the stubble, everyone does it this way now, saves diesel and time.

Yield — last few years my wheat gives maybe 900 jin per mu, maize 1100-1200 jin per mu when the weather is good. I expect about the same.
